title: Entropy-aware scroll groomer to reduce dashboard tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: A small but significant fraction of dashboard queries produces highly random access patterns (high entropy) across tenant time windows and offsets. These queries cause disproportionate tail latency due to many small disk/kv reads, cold micro-index lookups, and inability to leverage prefix/KV cache. Proposal: implement an "entropy-aware scroll groomer" that detects high-entropy scroll/pagination sessions and applies a lightweight grooming strategy: 1) ephemeral page coalescing (merge adjacent small pages server-side into a single read unit when contiguous keys/time ranges are detected), 2) on-demand micro-index consolidation for the session (temporarily materialize an in-memory compacted index for the session window), and 3) adaptive read hedging thresholds tuned by observed entropy and tenant priority. Goals: reduce 95th/99th percentile paginated query latency by >=25% for affected sessions while keeping median unchanged and limiting memory overhead to <=15% per affected worker. Design includes detection heuristics, grooming window sizing, eviction policy, cost accounting, and rollout flagging.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Patel: Filed initial ticket after review of SLO incidents. Observed correlated spikes during ad-hoc exploration by some large tenants. Attached sample trace excerpts (see attachments).

2025-02-11 - Liam O'Connor: Ran offline dataset scan on last 30 days; ~3.2% of paginated sessions qualify as 'high-entropy' by current metric (entropy > 0.85) but contribute ~18% of 99th percentile latency. Snapshot saved to GCS: gs://redwood-internal/entropy-scan/2025-02-11.csv

2025-02-12 - Engineering design sync: Chose ephemeral grooming over global reindex because it has lower operational blast radius. Agreed on three levers: page coalescing, micro-index consolidation, and read hedging. Liam to prototype coalescer; Priya to evaluate memory impact of micro-indexing in staging.

2025-02-14 - Prototype update (Liam): Implemented page coalescer that merges up to 4 contiguous pages with contiguous time/key ranges when backend reports sequential backing segments. Microbenchmark: affected synthetic session 95p latency reduced from 820ms to 540ms (34% improvement) on staging cluster with no cache warmup. CPU increased ~6%.

2025-02-15 - Design note (Priya Malhotra): Micro-index consolidation needs eviction TTL tied to session end and explicit accounting to tenant billing. Proposed default TTL 60s with config override. Potential tradeoff: memory fragmentation under many simultaneous exploratory sessions; mitigation: global groom concurrency limit (default 8 per worker).

2025-02-16 - Security check (Maya Chen): No additional data exposure; grooming uses existing read paths and does not persist consolidated indexes beyond TTL. Recommend flag disabled by default in Private deployments until KMS/secret review complete.

2025-02-17 - QA plan (QA Team): Create synthetic replay with 1k high-entropy sessions spread across tenants; validate 95p/99p latencies, memory, and error-rate. Add golden queries from customer X and Y to ensure functional parity.

2025-02-18 - Implementation note (Liam): Opening draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4827. Feature gated under 'entropy_scroll_groomer' with rollout percentage and per-tenant opt-out. Instrumented metrics: groom_sessions_total, groom_evictions_total, groom_memory_bytes, groom_latency_improvement_p95.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for identified high-entropy paginated sessions improves by >=25% in canary cluster
No increase >1% in overall error rate for dashboard query API during canary
Per-worker memory overhead for grooming stays below 15% on 99th percentile of runs
Feature is behind a runtime flag with per-tenant opt-out and rollout percentage control
Telemetry dashboards created: groom_sessions, groom_success_rate, latency_improvement_percentiles
